inputs.topic: Gradient Descent: how AI learns from mistakes

scene_count.evidence: The source explicitly expands the lesson to 12 compact beats because gradient descent needs a causal chain beyond the default 6-8 scenes. The scene plan covers promise, school slope, tracked AI example, prediction, numeric loss, loss-curve mapping, gradient direction, opposite update, new loss check, repetition, step-size risk, and recap.

mechanism_chain.evidence: The sequence continuously follows the mechanism: current weight W1 -> prediction dog 0.62 -> compare with cat target -> loss 8/10 -> W1 placed on loss curve -> local gradient points toward higher loss -> small opposite step to W2 -> new prediction and loss 5/10 -> repeat -> step-size comparison. Each step explains why the next step follows.

technical_completeness.evidence: The plan includes the required numeric and graph bridges: W1/W2 settings, dog/cat prediction scores, loss 8/10 and 5/10, loss-vs-setting curve, tangent, uphill gradient cue, opposite update arrow, repeated path, and overshoot example. It also avoids overclaiming: one update improves but does not finish learning, the curve is a simplified slice, and large steps can worsen loss.

opener_readiness.evidence: Scene 1 names the learning promise and visibly connects the familiar school slope notebook to an AI training tablet. A cold student can tell the lesson is about using slope to reduce prediction error in AI, and Scene 3 quickly introduces the concrete animal-classifier example before the mechanism begins.

renderer_readiness.evidence: The video blueprint and source table specify visible evidence, transformations, motion roles, risks, and a programmatic insert for the exact slope/update sequence. The absence of an image prompt pack is not a scene-flow defect at this gate; the approved scene flow is detailed enough to proceed to prompt writing for paired/native-plus-programmatic rendering.

false_completion_risk.evidence: The lesson prevents slogan-only understanding by requiring the learner to track the same object across the whole loop: W1 makes a wrong prediction, loss is scored, W1 becomes a graph point, gradient gives the uphill clue, the update moves opposite to W2, loss is checked again, and the process repeats. The step-size scene also blocks the false idea that any large downhill-looking move is better.

scene_notes.title: Learning promise
scene_notes.learning_job: Orient the learner to the school-math-to-AI-training connection.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: Lesson title, slope notebook, AI training tablet, bridge line from school graph to AI error reduction.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: School slope concept -> AI reducing prediction error.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: Could become a vague motivational hook if the slope-to-training bridge is not visible.

scene_notes.title: Familiar slope
scene_notes.learning_job: Refresh slope as a local direction clue on a curve.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: Simple curve in notebook with tangent and uphill/downhill arrows at one point.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: Point on curve -> local tangent/slope direction.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: Could turn into a derivative lesson if dense notation replaces the local clue.

scene_notes.title: Tiny AI task setup
scene_notes.learning_job: Introduce the single concrete example that will be tracked through training.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: Animal input card, tiny model panel, fixed target card labeled cat.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: Training example enters the model while the correct answer is held for comparison.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: If the animal example disappears later, the graph may feel disconnected.

scene_notes.title: Current setting makes prediction
scene_notes.learning_job: Show that the current model setting W1 causes the current output.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: W1 badge connected to prediction chips, dog 0.62, target cat visible.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: Current setting W1 + input -> prediction scores.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: Learner may think the wrong dog label appears randomly unless W1 is visibly connected to the output.

scene_notes.title: Mistake becomes loss
scene_notes.learning_job: Convert the prediction-target mismatch into a numeric error score.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: Gap between dog prediction and cat target feeding a loss meter labeled loss 8/10.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: Prediction vs correct target -> numeric loss score.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: Loss could look like an emotional warning rather than a computed wrongness score.

scene_notes.title: Loss depends on setting
scene_notes.learning_job: Explain why the lesson now uses a graph.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: Loss-vs-model-setting curve with W1 dot high on the curve, connected back to loss 8/10.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: Current setting W1 and its loss -> point on loss curve.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: The curve could appear as a random math visual if the W1-to-loss mapping is not shown.

scene_notes.title: Gradient clue
scene_notes.learning_job: Show that the local gradient points toward higher loss.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: Programmatic tablet graph with tangent at W1 and uphill cue labeled gradient: higher loss.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: Local slope at W1 -> direction where loss increases.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: A common false idea is that the gradient points downhill; this scene explicitly separates gradient/uphill from descent direction.

scene_notes.title: Opposite small update
scene_notes.learning_job: Show the core gradient descent update direction.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: Short arrow from W1 to nearby W2 opposite the gradient, with old and new points visible.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: W1 -> small step opposite gradient -> W2.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: If the arrow is too long or not clearly opposite, learners may miss why the update moves that way.

scene_notes.title: Check new loss
scene_notes.learning_job: Prove that the update changed the model and reduced loss without solving everything.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: W2 lower on curve, closer prediction cat 0.48 dog 0.44, loss meter 5/10, not perfect yet cue.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: New setting W2 -> new prediction -> lower loss compared with W1.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: Could imply one step completes training unless the imperfect prediction and repeat cue remain visible.

scene_notes.title: Repeat loop
scene_notes.learning_job: Show training as repeated measure-slope-step-check cycles.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: W2 becomes current, ordered loop strip, dotted descending path with check marks.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: One update result becomes the next starting point; repeated updates move toward lower loss.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: The dotted path could become decorative if the ordered checks are not shown.

scene_notes.title: Step-size quick check
scene_notes.learning_job: Compare careful small steps with an oversized update.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: Split graph showing small-step path descending and a huge arrow overshooting to higher loss.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: Small repeated updates vs one huge jump; huge jump lands at higher loss.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: Overshoot could look like faster progress unless the landing loss is visibly higher.

scene_notes.title: Memory anchor
scene_notes.learning_job: Make the mechanism retrievable as a concise loop.
scene_notes.visible_evidence: Four-step recap chain: measure loss -> read slope -> step opposite -> repeat.
scene_notes.transformation_or_comparison: Full mechanism compressed into an ordered recall diagram.
scene_notes.misconception_risk: Could become a slogan-only ending if the chain does not reuse the earlier W1/W2/loss visual language.

recommended_scene_flow: Learning promise: school slope connects to AI reducing prediction error.
Familiar slope: tangent at one point gives local rising direction.
Concrete AI task: one animal example enters a tiny classifier with target cat.
Current setting W1 makes the wrong prediction: dog 0.62 while target is cat.
W1 and loss 8/10 are mapped to a high point on a loss-vs-setting curve.
At W1, tangent/gradient shows the direction of higher loss.
Gradient descent takes a small step opposite the gradient from W1 to W2.
W2 is checked: prediction is closer and loss drops to 5/10, but not perfect.
Training repeats: new current point, measure loss, read slope, step opposite, check again.
Step-size check: small steps descend; one huge step can overshoot to higher loss.
Memory anchor: measure loss -> read slope -> step opposite -> repeat.
verdict.verdict: Clean scene adequacy pass. The planned 12-scene sequence is technically adequate because it tracks one concrete example through prediction, loss scoring, curve mapping, gradient direction, opposite update, lower-loss check, repetition, and step-size risk. It is ready for prompt writing and renderer-specific production planning.
